# Job Chapter 16 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folio 422r

---

**16:1** And-answered Iyyov [Job] and-said:

**16:2** "I-have-heard [shamati] many-things [rabbot] like-these; comforters of-trouble [menachamei amal] [are] all-of-you. **16:3** Is-there-an-end [ha-qets] to-words of-wind [ledivrei ruach]? Or what provokes-you [yamritsekha] that you-answer [ta'aneh]?

**16:4** Also I could-speak [adabberah] like-you; if [lu] your-soul [nafshekem] were in-the-place-of [tachat] my-soul [nafshi], I-could-string [achbirah] words [bemillin] against-you, and-shake [va'ani'ah] over-you with-my-head [bemori alekhem].

**16:5** I-would-strengthen-you [a'amitsekhem] with-my-mouth [bemo fi], and-the-comfort [nid] of-my-lips [sefatai] would-restrain [yachsokh] [your pain].

**16:6** If I-speak [adabberah], my-pain [ke'evi] is-not restrained [lo yechasekh]; and-if I-hold-back [vechedlah], what goes from-me [mah mimmeni yahalokh]?

**16:7** But now he-has-exhausted-me [hel'ani]; you-have-laid-waste [hashimmota] all my-company [adati]. **16:8** And-you-have-shriveled-me [vatiqqemeteni] — it-has-become a-witness [le-ed]; and-my-leanness [kachshi] rises-up [yaqom] against-me, it-testifies [ya'aneh] to-my-face [befanay].

**16:9** His-anger [appo] has-torn [taraf] and-he-persecutes-me [vayistemeni]; he-gnashes [charaq] upon-me with-his-teeth [shinnav]; my-adversary [tsarri] sharpens [yiltosh] his-eyes [einav] upon-me. **16:10** They-gape [pa'aru] upon-me with-their-mouth [pihem]; with-reproach [becherpah] they-strike [yakkuh] my-cheek [lechayay]; together [yachad] they-mass-themselves [yitmalleun] against-me.

**16:11** God [el] delivers-me [yasgireniy] to the-unjust [el avil], and-into the-hands of-the-wicked [reshaim] he-casts-me [yirteniy].

**16:12** At-ease [shalev] I-was and-he-shattered-me [vayefarpereni]; and-he-seized [ve'achaz] me-by-the-neck [be-orpi] and-he-dashed-me-to-pieces [vayefatseteni]; and-he-set-me-up [vayeqimeni] for-himself as-a-target [le-mattarah]. **16:13** His-archers [rabbav] surround-me [yasobbu]; he-splits [yefalach] my-kidneys [kilyotai] and-does-not spare [velo yachmol]; he-pours-out [yishpokh] my-gall [mererati] to-the-ground [la-arets].

**16:14** He-breaches-me [yifretseney] breach upon breach [perets al penei perets]; he-runs [yaruts] upon-me like-a-warrior [ke-gibbor].

**16:15** Sackcloth [saq] I-have-sewed [tafarti] upon my-skin [gildi], and-I-have-thrust [ve-olalti] my-horn [qarni] in-the-dust [be-afar]. **16:16** My-face [panai] is-red [chamarmerah] from weeping [min bekhi], and-upon my-eyelids [al afappai] [is] deep-shadow [tsalmaveth].

**16:17** Not [al] for-violence [chamas] in-my-hands [bekappai], and-my-prayer [tefillatiy] [is] pure [zakkah].

**16:18** O-earth [erets], do-not cover [al tekhassi] my-blood [dami], and-let-there-not be [al yehi] a-place [maqom] for-my-cry [le-za'aqati].

**16:19** Even [gam] now, behold, in-the-heavens [bashamayim] [is] my-witness [edi], and-my-advocate [sahadi] [is] on-high [bamromim]. **16:20** My-friends [meilitsai] [are] my-scorners [litsei]; to God [el eloah] my-eye [eini] drips [dallefah].

**16:21** And-he-would-argue [veyokach] for-a-man [le-gever] with God [im eloah], and-[between] a-son-of-man [uven adam] and-his-neighbor [le-re'ehu].

**16:22** For years of-number [shenot mispar] will-come [ye'etayu], and-[on] a-path [ve-orach] [of] no return [lo ashub] I-will-go [ehelokh]."

---
## EMET's Textual Notes

**v.2 — menachamei amal:** "Comforters of trouble" — a devastating wordplay. The friends came to comfort (*nacham*) but instead bring trouble (*amal*). The phrase is an oxymoron: their comfort itself is the affliction.

**v.9 — "His anger has torn":** Job describes God as a predatory animal — tearing, gnashing teeth, sharpening eyes. The violence of the imagery is unmatched in biblical prayer.

**v.12 — "he set me up as a target":** Hebrew *mattarah* — an archery target. God is the archer, Job the stationary mark. The image of divine violence continues with pierced kidneys and spilled gall (v.13).

**v.19 — sahadi:** "My advocate" — Aramaic loanword meaning "witness/testifier." Job appeals to a heavenly witness — distinct from God the adversary — who will testify on his behalf. This figure anticipates the *go'el* (redeemer) of 19:25.

**v.18 — "earth, do not cover my blood":** An echo of Genesis 4:10-11, where Abel's blood cries out from the ground. Job wants his suffering to remain visible, unburied, as perpetual testimony.

*— EMET*
